page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 256 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, requiring external block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core capabilities and memory throughput. The instance achieves high memory bandwidth, reaching 4103.87 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 277.75 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. It demonstrates strong performance in Passmark CPU tests, particularly in extended instructions and encryption, aided by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. Multi-core processing is further validated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17690.0 and a software compilation score of 41502.0.

Given its hardware profile, the n4-standard-64 is highly efficient for workloads that scale across many threads without requiring massive memory-to-core ratios or local NVMe drives. It is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, as evidenced by its 70.46 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and strong Passmark database scores. Additionally, the inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions enables efficient CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing where it handles 229.23 tokens per second on 7B models. Other suitable workloads include static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data decompression.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance configured with 64 vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, running on dedicated Intel x86_64 processors with 32 physical cores. It features a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lacks bundled local storage or GPUs. The architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel AMX and AVX-512, which drive strong performance in multi-core benchmarks, cryptography, and memory bandwidth. In testing, the instance demonstrated high efficiency in software compilation, database operations, and CPU-based LLM inference, achieving 70.46 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and strong prompt processing speeds. This profile makes the n4-standard-64 highly suitable for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, database hosting, static web serving, and moderate machine learning inference tasks.
